name: Low-flow priapism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Doppler Ultrasound Criteria for Low-flow Priapism

criteria.description: Erection lasting longer than 4 hours unrelated to sexual stimulation
Presence of painful, rigid penile erection
Cavernosal blood gas analysis showing hypoxia, hypercarbia, and acidosis
Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrating minimal or absent cavernosal arterial flow
No history of recent perineal or penile trauma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prolonged painful erection >4 hours plus cavernosal blood gas analysis consistent with ischemia and Doppler ultrasound showing absent or minimal arterial flow
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by cavernosal blood gas and Doppler ultrasound findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prolonged painful penile erection lasting over 4 hours

common.symptomName: Dark, hypoxic cavernosal blood on aspiration
searchTerms: low oxygen blood drawn from penis

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent cavernosal arterial flow on Doppler ultrasound
searchTerms: poor blood flow in penis on ultrasound
absent blood flow in penile arteries
loss of sensation in genital area

rare.symptomName: Sepsis secondary to penile tissue ischemia
searchTerms: blood infection from penile tissue damage

laboratory: Cavernosal blood gas showing hypoxia (pO2 <30 mmHg), hypercarbia (pCO2 >60 mmHg), and acidosis (pH <7.25)
Complete blood count to evaluate for underlying hematological disorders (e.g., sickle cell disease)
imaging: Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrating minimal or absent cavernosal arterial flow
Penile MRI (rarely used) to assess tissue viability
genetic: Genetic testing for sickle cell disease or other hemoglobinopathies if clinically indicated
other: Aspiration of dark, viscous cavernosal blood
Corporal smooth muscle biopsy in refractory cases

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or increased cavernosal arterial flow on Doppler ultrasound
Recurrent episodes of priapism with spontaneous resolution
Often associated with sickle cell disease
Shorter duration episodes compared to low-flow priapism

redFlags: Signs of penile tissue ischemia or necrosis
references: Montague DK, Jarow J, Broderick GA, et al. American Urological Association guideline on the management of priapism. J Urol. 2003;170(4 Pt 1):1318-1324.
Burnett AL, Bivalacqua TJ. Priapism: new concepts in medical and surgical management. Urol Clin North Am. 2011;38(4):185-194.
